findings.citation: non-enumerable and symbol keys are not inspected
findings.description: The assertDeep probe only uses plain enumerable string keys. Nothing checks that non-enumerable or symbol keys are ignored. Minor gap.

findings.citation: `withSummary` counts items whose trimmed summary is non-empty
findings.description: The held corpora have no whitespace-only summaries, and no probe sits on the 80-character boundary. Trimming and the threshold are never exercised. Also untested: a government source with no items, and an empty governmentSources list.
The deep-assertion check exercises only rank, arm, and matchedNorthStars; score, matched, and reasons are never passed to assertNothingEvaluative, and the constant itself is never inspected.

findings.citation: `assertNothingEvaluative(value: unknown): void` throws an `Error` if any object at any depth (including inside arrays) has an own enumerable string key (as listed by `Object.keys`) in `EVALUATIVE_KEYS`; non-enumerable and symbol keys are not inspected.
findings.description: No check distinguishes own enumerable string keys from inherited, non-enumerable, or symbol keys.

findings.citation: `blindItems(items: Item[], seed: number): BlindItem[]` returns, for every item, exactly `{ id, source, title, summary }` (summary `""` when absent), in seeded-shuffle order, and calls `assertNothingEvaluative` on its result before returning.
findings.description: The output is checked, but no check verifies that blindItems actually invokes the assertion before returning.

findings.citation: Three modules under `evals/relevance/`; all are pure functions over JSON data (no I/O).
findings.description: The scenarios inspect return values only and do not detect I/O or other side effects.

findings.citation: Keep the exported names and signatures from the specification.
findings.description: Runtime probes import only blindItems, assertNothingEvaluative, scoreArm, and auditCorpus; exported constants, helper APIs, interfaces, and TypeScript signatures are not checked.

findings.citation: `precisionAtK`: shown items with relevance ≥ 1, divided by `k`.
findings.description: Every scoring scenario has at least k ranked entries, so dividing by the number shown instead of k would pass.

findings.citation: `wrongReasons`: shown ids with relevance ≥ 1 and `reasonAccepted === false`, sorted ascending.
findings.description: No shown item combines relevance 0 with reasonAccepted false, so the relevance gate is not independently verified.

findings.citation: `withSummary` counts items whose trimmed summary is non-empty; `avgSummaryChars` is the mean trimmed length over those items, rounded to an integer (`0` when none); `topicsFromTitle` counts items with at least one topic whose every lower-cased topic is a token of the title (title lower-cased and split on runs of non-letters).
findings.description: Fixtures do not exercise surrounding summary whitespace, a fractional mean requiring rounding, empty topic arrays, or non-letter title separators other than spaces.

findings.citation: A government source is **starved** when fewer than half of its items have a trimmed summary of at least 80 characters.
findings.description: No scenario exercises an exactly-half source, an exactly-80-character summary, or whitespace affecting the 80-character threshold.
The supplied governmentSources order is already sorted in every audit scenario, so sorting is not verified.

findings.citation: `finding` is `"subject-matter-absent"` when every government source is starved, otherwise `"ranker-ordering"`.
findings.description: For an empty governmentSources array, the oracle adds a governmentSources.length > 0 guard and returns ranker-ordering, whereas the stated universal condition is true for every member of an empty set; no check resolves this discrepancy.

publicationScope: Admission judgments and native outcome metadata only; prompts, raw streams, HTTP bodies, configuration and credential state excluded.
